project.title: Δ-Potential Learning (ΔPL) for Protein Binding Affinity
project.goal: Train a cycle-consistent ΔΔG predictor for protein–protein and protein–ligand interfaces.
project.algorithm: Δ-Potential Learning parameterizes ΔΔG as f(σ→σ′, c) = h(σ′, c) − h(σ, c), where h : Σ × C → ℝ is a learned scalar potential. This enforces anti-symmetry, transitivity, and reflexivity exactly by construction, rather than as soft penalties. Theoretical sample complexity drops from O(|Σ|²·d/ε²) to O(|Σ|·d/ε²).

## 1. StaB-ddG: did they train on the data we're testing on?

**Yes — and here's the exact scope of the leakage:**

- **StaB-ddG was trained on SKEMPI.** They split SKEMPI into 119 train PDBs + 81 test PDBs using **interface-homology clustering** (homologous structures stay together). Their 1491-item published test set comes from those 81 test PDBs.
- **Our 5-fold GroupKFold is by individual PDB, not by cluster.** For our OOF predictions, the model that predicted item X had never seen X's exact PDB in training. **PDB-level: leakage-free.**
- **BUT** — leakage audit just confirmed at 30% identity: **100% of StaB-ddG's 81 test PDBs have at least one homolog in our training data.** So our OOF predictions on the StaB test slice are NOT cluster-leakage-free. The model could be picking up on homologous training PDBs.

## 1. Why DPL "sucks" vs Unconstrained on stability

The DPL model parameterizes $f(c, a, b) = \sum_i [h_\theta(b_i, c_i) - h_\theta(a_i, c_i)]$. This is **additive across sites** and **anti-symmetric in (wt, mt)**. The sample-complexity advantage comes from this being a much smaller hypothesis class. But that prior is only a free lunch when the underlying physics actually has that structure. Here's what's different about FireProt vs SKEMPI:

| | SKEMPI binding | FireProt stability |
|---|---|---|
| Mutations live at | a protein-protein **interface** | the **monomeric core** |
| Number of unique proteins | 297 | **125** (much fewer) |
| Mutations per protein | ~26 | **~40** |
| Context $c_i$ varies across | many different complexes | mostly the same fold |
